title: Query performance measurement harness (foundational)
description: Signature original: A harness runs a representative query workload against the current index and records latency and recall per query. The workload is sampled from real retrieval history so measurements reflect actual use, not synthetic benchmarks. Every measurement is timestamped and stored for trend analysis. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import time
workload = ['index latency', 'posting lists', 'hash verify']
for q in workload:
    t0 = time.perf_counter(); time.sleep(0.001); dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print(f'{q}: {dt*1000:.2f}ms')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Self-Improving Index Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Index variant A/B testing (foundational)
description: Signature original: Candidate index structures are built side by side and tested on the same workload, with each variant measured independently. The comparison uses paired statistics so query-to-query variance does not masquerade as a structural difference. Only a variant that wins significantly replaces the incumbent. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Self-Improving Index Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Structure selection by workload fit (foundational)
description: Signature original: The builder selects index structures by workload characteristics: point lookups favor hash indexes, range scans favor trees, text search favors inverted indexes. Selection rules are explicit and reviewable, not learned black boxes. Mixed workloads get composite structures with a routing layer. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
workload = {'point_lookup': 0.7, 'range_scan': 0.2, 'text': 0.1}
choice = max(workload, key=workload.get)
print('dominant pattern:', choice, '-> recommend hash index')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Self-Improving Index Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Incremental index rebuild (foundational)
description: Signature original: When the structure changes, the index rebuilds incrementally: new writes go to the new structure while old segments migrate in the background. Incremental rebuild keeps the archive searchable throughout the transition. A cutover flag flips reads to the new structure only after verification passes. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
segments, migrated = 10, 0
while migrated < segments:
    migrated += 2  # background migration batches
print(f'migrated {migrated}/{segments} segments | reads still on old index until verified')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Self-Improving Index Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Improvement tracking dashboard data (foundational)
description: Signature original: Every rebuild records before-and-after metrics: mean latency, p99 latency, recall, and index size. The tracking history proves whether the builder's changes actually helped over time. Regressions trigger automatic rollback to the previous structure. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
hist = [{'ver': 'v1', 'p99': 900}, {'ver': 'v2', 'p99': 320}]
print('p99 improvement:', hist[0]['p99'], '->', hist[1]['p99'], 'ms')
print('rollback' if hist[-1]['p99'] > hist[-2]['p99'] else 'keep v2')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Self-Improving Index Builder, 2026-10-21.
